- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to account for bearish sentiment bias.  
- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model often overestimates; reduce forecast peak values to avoid overshoot.  
- When price has recently spiked upward, model frequently overcorrects with a sharp drop; add a lagged smoothing factor to dampen immediate reversal.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after a peak), model often fails to anticipate; adjust forecast to reflect slower decay.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price in early days of the forecast window; apply a small upward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
